content: The comparison of the comparator group (n=44) in this study revealed an imbalance in the measured characteristics of the participants. Despite random allocation to treatment groups, imbalances were observed in prior tuberculosis (TB) treatment, smear status, and the prevalence of fluoroquinolone-resistant TB (pre-XDR TB) at baseline. This imbalance suggests the presence of unmeasured confounding factors. Consequently, the certainty of the evidence was downgraded by one level due to the unmeasured confounding, which likely arose from the small sample size. The ZENIX study was conducted in the Russian Federation, the Republic of Moldova, and South Africa. These settings may not be representative of other populations where multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) is prevalent. However, since the study was conducted in three countries, enhancing its generalizability, the certainty of the evidence was not downgraded for indirectness. The small number of participants in both the intervention group (n=43) and the comparator group (n=44) poses a very serious risk of imprecision. As a result, the certainty of the evidence was downgraded by two levels. The TB PRACTECAL study (BPaL arm) was compared with the ZENIX study (1200–26 arm). In this comparison, participants were not randomly allocated to either group, and the settings and eligibility criteria of the studies differed. Significant differences in baseline characteristics, including gender, HIV status, prior TB treatment, prior drug-resistant TB treatment, smear positivity, and fluoroquinolone-resistant TB, were noted. Although adjustments were made for measured confounding, the imbalance between groups indicates the likely presence of unmeasured confounding. Therefore, the certainty of the evidence was downgraded by two levels. The ZENIX study was conducted in the Russian Federation, the Republic of Moldova, and South Africa, while TB PRACTECAL was conducted in South Africa, Uzbekistan, and Belarus. These settings may not fully represent other populations where MDR-TB is common. However, since the studies were conducted in five countries, increasing their generalizability, the certainty of the evidence was not downgraded for indirectness. The small number of participants in both the intervention group (n=43) and the comparator group (n=44) results in a very serious risk of imprecision. Consequently, the certainty of the evidence was downgraded by two levels. In the ZENIX study, participants, trial investigators, and staff (including laboratory staff) were blinded to the dose and scheduled duration of linezolid. However, participants were unblinded to the use of bedaquiline and pretomanid. This comparison involved one arm of ZENIX and the WHO short (SA 2017) cohort, which was a non-randomized comparison. Therefore, the certainty of the evidence was not downgraded due to the partial blinding of ZENIX. Baseline imbalances were observed in age, gender, HIV status, prior TB and drug-resistant TB history, smear status, and culture positivity between the two groups. In most comparisons, adjustments for measured confounding were not possible due to the small number of events in the intervention group (<5 individuals with a positive or negative outcome). This suggests the likely presence of confounding bias. The imbalance in measured covariates also indicates the likelihood of unmeasured confounding. As the WHO IPD data were collected under programmatic conditions, there is a significant potential to underestimate relapse due to missing follow-up details. Misclassification of death during the follow-up period is also possible, as there is no death registry to link to cohort data for deaths occurring after treatment completion. Considerable variability was observed in the effect estimates between cohorts in the comparator group. The overall effect in the comparator group is strongly influenced by a small number of larger cohorts, which have varying effect estimates. The ZENIX study was a clinical trial conducted in the Russian Federation, the Republic of Moldova, and South Africa. The procedures within the trial in these settings may not be comparable to those used in other programmatic settings where MDR-TB commonly occurs. Given the important differences between a trial and programmatic settings, the certainty of the evidence was downgraded for indirectness. The small number of participants in both the intervention group (n=43) and the comparator group (n=44) results in a very serious risk of imprecision. Consequently, the certainty of the evidence was downgraded by two levels. Baseline imbalances were observed in gender, HIV status, prior TB treatment, smear status, culture positivity, and fluoroquinolone resistance status between the two groups. In all comparisons, adjustments for measured confounding were not possible due to the small number of events in the intervention group (<5 individuals with a positive or negative outcome). This suggests the likely presence of confounding bias. The substantial imbalance in measured covariates also indicates the likelihood of unmeasured confounding. As the SA 2019 cohort data were collected under programmatic conditions, there is a significant potential to underestimate relapse due to missing follow-up details. Misclassification of death during the follow-up period is also possible, although deaths reported in the South African death registry were linked to participant follow-up data using a national identification number. The ZENIX study (intervention arm) was a clinical trial conducted in the Russian Federation, the Republic of Moldova, and South Africa. The procedures within the trial in these settings may not be comparable to those used in other programmatic settings where MDR-TB commonly occurs. Given the important differences between a trial and programmatic settings, the certainty of the evidence was downgraded for indirectness. The small number of participants in both the intervention group (n=43) and the comparator group (n=44) results in a very serious risk of imprecision. Consequently, the certainty of the evidence was downgraded by two levels.
